title: Adaptive prioritization playbook for hosted API enterprise intake (chat, streaming, toolcalls, structured outputs)
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit high-signal but heterogeneous feature requests to the hosted API intake (multi-turn chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs). Current funnel overloads PMs and delays responses; small surface-area requests get mixed with high-risk enterprise asks requiring SLA and security reviews. Goal: build an adaptive prioritization playbook that converts incoming requests into standardized intake records, scores them across risk/benefit/cost axes, surfaces required compliance checks early, and produces a deterministic routing decision (self-serve backlog, PM fast-track, enterprise sales handoff, or immediate engineering spike).

Scope: inbound non-bug feature requests only (no incidents). Cover chat streaming, toolcalls/function-calls, structured outputs, and multi-modal request variants. Deliverables: prioritization rubric, required signal checklist, intake form templates, routing rules, and a 30/60/90 rollout plan including metrics and runbook for exceptions.

Why now: increasing enterprise volume and repeated delays for requests that affect SLAs, security posture, or Dedicated/Private product modes. Standardization will reduce TTR for high-impact asks and ensure correct downstream workflows (security review, Dedicated sizing, roadmap planning).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented prioritization rubric that scores every inbound request on customer impact, engineering effort estimate band, security/compliance flag, and business value. 2) Intake form templates (Confluence + web form) with required fields that automatically flag security_review_required. 3) Routing rules implemented as a decision table with clear outputs: Backlog, PM Fast-Track, Sales/EarlyAccess, Eng Spike. 4) Pilot on 20 enterprise requests with median triage time <= 48 hours and >80% correct routing verified by stakeholder audit. 5) Playbook handed off to Ops with runbook and escalation paths.
comments: 2026-01-22: Initial intake from Solutions (customer: MediScribe) saw a 12-day triage delay — triggered project proposal (Maya).
2026-01-29: Scoping workshop with Eng (Priya, Jules), Design (Rae) and Security (Nima). Agreed on four signal axes: impact, cost, compliance, and strategic fit.
2026-02-10: Draft rubric v0 created. Engineering asked to include an 'estimated infra delta' band (negligible/moderate/significant) for Dedicated/private sizing implications.
2026-02-18: Product review: decided to require 'data residency' and 'PII exposure' checkbox on intake form; these auto-trigger security review flag.
2026-02-26: Design delivered web intake mockups (Confluence link in links). PM requested validation for minimum fields to avoid friction.
2026-03-03: Ran a small classifier spike with Solutions signals (ENG-23344) to auto-populate candidate labels; engineering estimates for integration ~3 points.
2026-03-08: Stakeholder demo: Sales and Customer Success accepted routing outputs but asked for an optional 'customer timeline' field to increase fidelity for prioritization.
2026-03-10: Decision to pilot the playbook with 20 incoming enterprise requests starting 2026-03-15. Assigned Ops lead: Lina Torres. Next: create pilot dashboard and audit checklist.
next_steps: 1) Finalize intake form and automation hooks (Due 2026-03-12). 2) Engineering to implement minimal classifier integration and decision-table (ENG spike run by 2026-03-20). 3) Ops to build pilot dashboard and audit workflow. 4) Run 2-week pilot and collect metrics; review 2026-04-05.
